summary: 1937 CCC-built 100-foot Aermotor fire tower near Delmar, Lowndes County, Georgia; GFC-administered and NHLR-registered 2021; in active use as of 2020.

facts.design: 100-foot steel Aermotor tower with a 7 by 7 foot cab

access.note: The NHLR says the tower was in active use as of 2020 because of restricted airspace around Moody Air Force Base. No public visit information was found.

visit.trail_note: No public visit route found. Check with the Georgia Forestry Commission before visiting.

events.note: Built with CCC labor; construction sponsored by the Grand Bay Timber Protective Association. A 1937 newspaper item says construction had begun.
Wooden steps replaced by Georgia Forestry Commission personnel
Windows replaced and exterior repainted by contractors
Registered January 8, 2021 as US 1474, GA 28; nominated by Angela Kufrovich

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR gives 218 ft (66 m). A Georgia tower list gives 215 ft. The record's elevation_m of 66.4 follows the NHLR; the story gives both figures.

notes_for_editor: The newest status in any source read is from 2020 (NHLR), so current access is unverified. The 1937 newspaper item is known only through the Forest Lookouts quote; the newspaper itself was not read. The Moody AFB airspace explanation is the NHLR's, not checked against Air Force sources. No staffing or fire history found. Record aliases include 'lowndes'.
